comparison: Both evaluate bulk RNA-seq findings (C42-C46). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical methods. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting clarification on differential gene analysis methods and expressing confusion about logistic regression interpretations in Table 3.

Both address therapeutic implications (C74). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of intervention studies and insufficient support for medication ineffectiveness claims. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, not objecting to therapeutic target discussion while requesting tempering of causal claims elsewhere.

Both evaluate integrative conclusions about CD8+ Trm cells as disease drivers (C52-C54, C56, C70, C72-C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes causal language exceeds correlative data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting to 'temper claims about CD8 Trms being drivers' and emphasize them as 'defining feature' rather than 'mechanistic driver.'

Both evaluate cohort demographics and clinical characteristics (C39-C41, C85-C87). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate sample size, noting age difference as potential confounder. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting cohort data without challenge to demographic characterization, though requesting analytical clarification.

Both address medication ineffectiveness claims (C68-C69). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting lack of detail on medications and absence of direct experimental evidence for claims about CD8+ Trm eradication. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the clinical observation without challenge.

Both evaluate spatial transcriptomics findings (C31-C33, C37-C38). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to n=1 EOLP sample limiting generalizability. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting 'n>1 per group when comparing groups (EOLP)' and questioning IL-23 production interpretation and focus on specific genes.

Both evaluate cytokine production data (C4, C51, C64). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by ELISA data with appropriate methods, though notes unclear significance for some cytokines. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging cytokine production findings from ELISA or gene expression analyses.

Both address cell composition differences (C14-C18). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with consistent scRNA-seq data but notes small EOLP sample size (n=2) limits generalizability. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the findings while requesting commentary on roles of B cells and mast cells in pathogenesis.

Both evaluate spatial distribution patterns (C2, C34-C36, C71). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by spatial transcriptomics with appropriate co-localization methods, though notes single EOLP sample limitation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging valuable contribution without challenging spatial or quantitative findings.

Both address NK/T cell subclustering and proportional differences (C20-C21). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear marker-based identification and data-driven differential proportions. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, requesting improved display and methods detail but not challenging cell identification or proportional differences.

Both evaluate cytokine receptor expression in spatial data (C37-C38). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes single EOLP sample limits robustness. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with broader concerns about n=1 sample size and questioning specific gene focus and IL-23 production claims.

Both address validation experiments (C90-C91, C98-C99, C100). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry with convergent methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN specifically for flow cytometry due to unclear gating strategy and labeling issues preventing data interpretation, though immunofluorescence not specifically challenged.

Both evaluate gene expression patterns in T cells (C22-C24). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by scRNA-seq data with well-established functional annotations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, requesting figure presentation clarification but not challenging gene expression findings themselves.

Both address basic scRNA-seq dataset characteristics (C11-C13, C92). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with consistent data and clear pipeline, noting small EOLP sample size limitation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, requesting improved presentation and methods detail but accepting basic dataset characteristics and cell type identification.

Both evaluate immunofluorescence validation of spatial findings (C3, C47-C50). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by orthogonal validation with multiple convergent methods. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging solid data and valuable contribution without challenging spatial distribution or quantitative findings.

Both address differential expression and GO enrichment in CD8+ T cells (C26-C27, C29). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by convergent analytical approaches strengthening conclusions. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, requesting methodological clarification on figure details but accepting gene expression data.

Both evaluate pseudotime trajectory analysis (C30, C55). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by multiple analytical approaches, noting pseudotime infers relationships that may not reflect actual temporal dynamics. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenging pseudotime analysis or interpretation.

Both address longitudinal follow-up design and outcomes (C88-C89). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate design and clear outcome definitions. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting cohort establishment and clinical characterization without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background literature claims (C1, C5-C10, C58-C67, C77-C84) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R11 addresses only C77-C78 as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether erosive vs. non-erosive represents distinct disease states or a spectrum, suggesting EOLP may be more severe presentation of same disease.

Minimal overlap on C25 (gene expression). OpenEval R3 finds gene expression patterns SUPPORTED by scRNA-seq with well-established functional annotations. Peer R2 accepts cytokine-related findings including gene expression without challenge.

Minimal overlap on C28 (enhanced CD8+ Trm activity). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by convergent analytical approaches. Peer reviewers accept cytokine production and related functional findings without challenge.

Minimal overlap on C100 (mechanistic inference about cytokine production). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic inference is reasonable yet not definitively proven. Peer R14 rates validation experiments UNCERTAIN due to flow cytometry presentation issues preventing interpretation.

OpenEval R2 evaluates NK/T cell clustering rationale and marker-based identification (C19, C75-C76) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims about initial clustering approach.

OpenEval R6 evaluates spatial co-localization methodology (C97) as SUPPORTED with appropriate marker gene approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this methodological claim, though related spatial findings are evaluated in peer R1.
